title: Implementation of Anemia Mukt Bharat Abhiyaan Operational Guidelines
subtitle:
Anemia Mukt Bharat Abhiyaan Unveils 7X7X7 Framework to Accelerate Anemia Reduction
New Anemia Mukt Bharat Abhiyaan Guidelines Focus on Testing, Treatment, Tracking and Dietary Diversification
body_text:
The Government of India has recently released the Anemia Mukt Bharat Abhiyaan Operational guidelines during the 16 th Central Council of Health and Family Welfare (CCHFW) meeting on 29 th June 2026 to address anemia through a 7X7X7 strategy, moving ahead from the older 6X6X6 strategy of Anemia Mukt Bharat programme. The components of Anemia Mukt Bharat Abhiyaan are:
Saturation of Hb testing using Digital Invasive Hemoglobinometers at platforms based on beneficiary group. P rophylaxis and targeted therapeutic management as per category of anemia diagnosed. Segregation of nutritional anemia and non-nutritional anemia for appropriate case-base management. Robust digital system for tracking anemia services: Shift from T3 approach (Test, Treat, Talk) toward T4 approach (Test, Treat, Talk and Track) Dietary diversification with Eat Right Approach and promotion of locally available iron rich foods on everyday basis. Implementation of convergent approach- ‘whole of Government Approach’ for implementation of complementary interventions, inter-ministerial convergence ‘Jan Bhagidari- Communication strategy for transformation of mindset from passive acceptance of anemia to active ownership (for Test, Treat, Talk and Track)
The details of 7X7X7 framework under Anemia Mukt Bharat Abhiyaan are as follows:
The seven beneficiaries are:
Children 6-59 months Children 5-9 years Adolescents 10-19 years Pregnant women Lactating mothers Women in reproductive age (20-49 years) 0-6 months LBW babies
The seven interventions are:
Prophylactic IFA Supplementation Testing of anemia Therapeutic management of anemia Deworming and Delayed Cord Clamping Jan Bhagidari- communication strategy to counteract normalised perception of anemia and improve compliance to IFA supplementation Addressing non-nutritional causes of anemia Eating Right – promotion of locally available iron rich food and diet diversification
The seven Institutional mechanisms are:
Intra-ministerial coordination National Centre of Excellence and Advanced Research on Anemia National AMB Abhiyaan Unit Strengthening supply chain and logistics Convergence with other Ministries Anemia Mukt Bharat Abhiyaan Portal Digital Framework for monitoring through T4 approach
The T4 approach includes Testing for anemia, Treatment for anemia, Talk for awareness and compliance through Jan Bhagidari, and Tracking the beneficiaries for treatment, referral and follow-up. The digital framework has been entailed under Anemia Mukt Bharat Abhiyaan to record, strengthen digital tracking and monitoring of anemia services. The beneficiaries are tested for anemia across platforms, pregnant and lactating mothers registered in JANANI Portal, school going children registered in RBSK portal and children for vaccination registered in U-WIN portal. The categorization of anemia into mild, moderate and severe anemia and appropriate management of anemia as per protocols is envisioned under Anemia Mukt Bharat Abhiyaan.
The Union Minister of State for Health and Family Welfare, Smt. Anupriya Patel stated this in a written reply in the Rajya Sabha today.

ministry.name: Ministry of Health and Family Welfare

enrichment.summary: The Ministry of Health and Family Welfare has released Operational Guidelines for the Anemia Mukt Bharat (AMB) Abhiyaan, introducing an upgraded '7X7X7' framework that replaces the earlier '6X6X6' strategy. The new framework covers seven beneficiary groups, seven interventions, and seven institutional mechanisms, with a shift from the 'T3' (Test, Treat, Talk) approach to a 'T4' approach (Test, Treat, Talk and Track) for digital monitoring. This was stated by Union Minister of State for Health and Family Welfare, Smt. Anupriya Patel, in a written reply in the Rajya Sabha on 11 August 2026.
enrichment.context:
Anemia Mukt Bharat was launched in 2018 under the National Health Mission as one of the six flagship components of India's nutrition strategy, aiming to reduce anemia prevalence among women, children, and adolescents through the earlier 6X6X6 strategy (six target beneficiary groups, six interventions, six institutional mechanisms). Anemia remains a major public health challenge in India, with National Family Health Survey (NFHS-5) data showing high prevalence among children, adolescent girls, and pregnant women, contributing to poor maternal and child health outcomes, low birth weight, and reduced productivity. The revised 7X7X7 framework, unveiled during the 16th Central Council of Health and Family Welfare meeting, expands the beneficiary base to include 0-6 month low birth weight babies, and introduces greater granularity by distinguishing nutritional from non-nutritional causes of anemia for tailored clinical management.

The move toward a 'T4' approach (adding 'Track' to the earlier Test-Treat-Talk model) reflects a broader governmental push toward digital health governance, integrating anemia surveillance with existing digital platforms such as JANANI (for pregnant and lactating women), RBSK (Rashtriya Bal Swasthya Karyakram, for school children), and U-WIN (vaccination tracking). This digital convergence is part of the Ayushman Bharat Digital Mission's vision of interoperable health records and real-time tracking of health interventions. The emphasis on 'Jan Bhagidari' (public participation) also aligns with the government's broader strategy of behavioral change communication seen in other health and sanitation programmes, aiming to shift anemia from a normalized, passively accepted condition to one actively managed by beneficiaries and communities. The 'whole of government' convergence approach signals recognition that anemia reduction requires action beyond health ministries alone, involving food security, women and child development, and rural development sectors.

prelims_questions.question: The 'Anemia Mukt Bharat Abhiyaan' 7X7X7 framework, as per recently released operational guidelines, includes which of the following components?
options: Seven beneficiary groups, seven interventions, and seven institutional mechanisms
Seven states, seven districts, and seven blocks for pilot implementation
Seven types of iron supplements distributed free of cost
Seven private hospital chains partnering for anemia treatment
prelims_questions.explanation: The release explicitly describes the 7X7X7 framework as consisting of seven beneficiary groups, seven interventions, and seven institutional mechanisms under the Anemia Mukt Bharat Abhiyaan.

prelims_questions.question: Under the Anemia Mukt Bharat Abhiyaan's digital tracking framework, which of the following portals is used to register school-going children for anemia testing?
prelims_questions.explanation: As per the release, school-going children are registered in the RBSK (Rashtriya Bal Swasthya Karyakram) portal, while pregnant and lactating mothers use JANANI and children for vaccination use U-WIN.
